recommendation_rationale: Best risk balance for a 40-person Dublin agency: EU (Frankfurt) hosting option, low adoption risk, moderate lock-in; mitigations: select EU data residency at portal creation, run a transfer impact assessment for US subprocessors, quarterly full data export as exit hedge.
gdpr_posture_salesforce: Strongest formal posture: EU data centres and Hyperforce EU Operating Zone, mature DPA/SCCs/BCRs; residency guarantees may require specific editions/add-ons. Residual risk: low.
gdpr_posture_hubspot: EU data hosting (Frankfurt) selectable only at portal creation; relies on EU-US Data Privacy Framework for US subprocessors; good DPA and consent tooling. Residual risk: low-medium.
gdpr_posture_zoho: EU data centres (Amsterdam, Dublin) selectable at signup; privacy-forward model but weaker compliance documentation and subprocessor transparency; India/US group entities require TIA. Residual risk: medium.
lock_in_salesforce: High: proprietary metadata/Apex, multi-year auto-renewing contracts with uplift clauses; exit needs consultant help, 2-4 months.
lock_in_hubspot: Medium: good CSV/API exports but workflows/reports/assets do not port; annual prepay; exit 4-8 weeks.
lock_in_zoho: Low-moderate: monthly billing available, full data export, modest customisation surface.
migration_risk_summary: Data import is easy for all three; process migration (pipelines, ad-ops integrations, email sync) is the real risk. Salesforce highest (needs paid partner ~EUR 10-30k plus part-time admin), HubSpot lowest, Zoho middle (UX sprawl drives shadow spreadsheets).
hidden_cost_risk_summary: Salesforce add-ons and renewal uplifts can double headline price; HubSpot marketing-contact tiers and Hub bundling cause step-change cost jumps plus mandatory onboarding fees; Zoho cheapest headline but bundle upsell and internal configuration time.
support_risk_summary: Salesforce slow without paid Premier (30% uplift), partner-dependent; HubSpot good included support with EU-hours coverage on Professional; Zoho weakest support (latency, escalation friction), partly offset by low cost and Dublin presence.

risk_register.risk: Implementation cost/complexity overrun; adoption stalls without dedicated admin or paid partner
risk_register.mitigation: If chosen, fix-price the implementation with a certified partner, budget a part-time admin, and pilot with one team before full rollout.

risk_register.risk: Multi-year contract lock-in with auto-renewal price uplifts and high exit cost
risk_register.mitigation: Negotiate renewal caps and termination terms pre-signature; schedule weekly data exports; avoid Apex customisation where config suffices.

risk_register.risk: Hidden add-on costs (API limits, support uplift, marketing add-ons) doubling headline price
risk_register.mitigation: Build a 3-year TCO including add-ons before contract; cap scope to core Sales Cloud.

risk_register.risk: Portal created in US region by default; EU data residency cannot be switched later without portal migration
risk_register.mitigation: Explicitly select EU (Frankfurt) data hosting at portal creation; verify region in account settings before any data import.

risk_register.risk: Cost creep from marketing-contact tiers and forced Hub bundling at renewal
risk_register.mitigation: Model contact growth for 3 years; use non-marketing contact flagging; negotiate tier pricing annually.

risk_register.risk: US parent / US subprocessors create Schrems II transfer exposure if DPF is invalidated
risk_register.mitigation: Document a transfer impact assessment, sign SCC fallback in the DPA, minimise special-category data in CRM.

risk_register.risk: Workflows, reports and marketing assets non-portable at exit
risk_register.mitigation: Quarterly full export to Brightline-controlled storage; document key workflows outside the tool.

risk_register.risk: Weak support SLAs and escalation friction delay incident resolution
risk_register.mitigation: Buy a paid support tier; keep an internal power-user; test support responsiveness during trial.

risk_register.risk: Less mature compliance documentation and subprocessor transparency complicates GDPR accountability
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain DPA, audit reports, and subprocessor list pre-contract; confirm EU DC selection at signup; record processing in Brightline's ROPA.

risk_register.risk: UX inconsistency across module sprawl drives low adoption and shadow spreadsheets
risk_register.mitigation: Restrict rollout to CRM core modules, invest in 2-3 training sessions, monitor login/usage metrics monthly.

assumptions: Knowledge-only analysis (no web access); vendor terms, data-centre footprints and DPF status as of early-2026 training data - verify before signature.
Brightline is an Irish GDPR data controller with ~40 seats, no in-house DPO or large IT team.
CRM will hold client and prospect personal data but no special-category data.
